description: 90th in the July 2026 Henley Passport Index, down one place, with 44 destinations reachable visa-free or visa-on-arrival. Other indices differ by method: Passport Index lists 25 visa-free with a power rank of 91, and VisaGuide places Nigeria 189th of 199 with 28.
energy_note: Forty-four doors, out of roughly two hundred.

aspect: The long trend is the real story
description: Nigeria has fallen roughly 26 places in twenty years, from 62nd in 2006. One tracker records a drop from 46 destinations in January 2025 to 44 in May 2026 - the number shrinking rather than growing.
energy_note: Twenty-six places down in twenty years.

aspect: Regional peers do better, which removes the easy explanation
description: Ghana and Senegal rank higher through broader bilateral arrangements in South America and Asia. The constraint is diplomatic and reputational, not geographic or continental.
energy_note: Not an Africa problem. A Nigeria problem.

aspect: Every closed door is an application
description: Each destination not on the list means a fee, an appointment, documents, a wait and a refusal risk - so the passport's weakness converts directly into the costs recorded in VIS-001.
energy_note: The ranking is a bill, paid per trip.

aspect: SCENARIO - the destinations that are not destinations
description: The forty-four include several she will never go to and excludes every country she has professional reason to visit. The headline number is not a measure of where she can go; it is a measure of where nobody objects to her going.
energy_note: Forty-four places, and none of them the conference.
